source_statement: Gr^kB approx Gr^kA direct-sum Gr^(k-1)A.M1 direct-sum ... direct-sum Gr^0A.Mk.
coordinates: B=A[Y1,Y2,...], Yj=gamma^jX, wt(Yj)=j; every polynomial has a unique finite expansion sum_m a_m m. This is the gamma-coordinate identification of4.3/4.10.

coefficient_test.notation: For this proof only, H^k is the set of finite expansions with a_m in Fil^{max(k-wt(m),0)}A. No altered4.12 statement is inserted into either source layer.
coefficient_test.multiplication: The coefficient of mn in a_m m times b_n n lies in Fil^{max(p-wt(m),0)+max(q-wt(n),0)}A, contained in Fil^{max(p+q-wt(mn),0)}A. Consequently H^p H^q is contained in H^{p+q}; H^0=B and every H^k is an ideal.
coefficient_test.gamma_of_monomial: For a positive-weight monomial m, iterated product polynomials P-prime_r express gamma^r(m) in gamma^l(Yj). Every such P-prime term has total input-index weight at least r by3.5. The Q-prime_(j,l) expression of gamma^l(Yj) has gamma-coordinate weight at least l by3.6. Substitution therefore gives only monomials of weight at least r, so gamma^r(m) belongs to H^r.
coefficient_test.gamma_of_coefficient_times_monomial: Apply4.11 through the actual A-lambda-homomorphism B→B sending X to m. A term of gamma-input weight n in gamma^r(aX) has coefficient in Fil^{max(r-n,0)}A. Its substituted product of gamma^j(m) lies in H^n by the preceding step. The term is in H^r, and so is gamma^r(am).
coefficient_test.gamma_of_general_augmentation_zero_eleme: Write b=a0+sum_{m positive} a_m m. Its augmentation is epsilon_A(a0), hence epsilon_B(b)=0 gives epsilon_A(a0)=0. Additivity gamma_t(b)=gamma_t(a0) product_m gamma_t(a_m m), together with gamma^r(a0) in Fil^rA and the previous step, gives gamma^r(b) in H^r. Definition3.10.1 and the ideal/product properties then give Fil^kB contained in H^k.
coefficient_test.reverse_inclusion: A monomial m of weight w is a product of gamma^j(X) with total index w, hence belongs to Fil^wB. The inclusion A→B preserves the canonical filtrations by3.10. For w<=k, a_m in Fil^{k-w}A implies a_m m in Fil^kB. For w>=k, m is already in Fil^kB and multiplication by every a_m is allowed. Thus H^k is contained in Fil^kB.
coefficient_test.result: The coefficient test is proved in both directions directly from the preceding definitions and polynomial identities.

forward_map: For 0<=i<=k and m in M_i, send [a]m with a in Fil^{k-i}A to [am] in Fil^kB/Fil^{k+1}B.
forward_well_defined: Changing a by Fil^{k+1-i}A changes am by Fil^{k+1}B.
inverse_map: For [b] in Gr^kB, expand b=sum a_m m uniquely. For each wt(m)=i<=k, take [a_m] in Fil^{k-i}A/Fil^{k+1-i}A; discard terms of weight greater than k.
inverse_well_defined: The proved coefficient test for Fil^{k+1}B shows that every coefficient of a change of representative has zero indicated class. Terms of weight greater than k belong to Fil^{k+1}B.
compositions: The inverse after the forward map returns the same monomial and coefficient class. The forward map after the inverse differs from b only by coefficient changes and weight>k terms in Fil^{k+1}B. Both compositions are identities.
scope: This establishes the printed graded formula and the monomial-coefficient implication in4.13(i). It does not make the printed4.12 finite tail contain Y3 at k=1, and no replacement theorem or source-body emendation is proposed.
